title: Diagnostic criteria for post–polycythaemia vera myelofibrosis
copyright: Adapted, with permission, from: Barosi G, Mesa RA, Thiele J, et al. Proposed criteria for the diagnosis of post-polycythemia vera and post-essential thrombocythemia myelofibrosis: a consensus statement from the International Working Group for Myelofibrosis Research and Treatment. Leukemia. 2008 Feb;22(2):437–8. PMID:17728787.
tablehtml:
Required criteria:

·   Documentation of a previous diagnosis of WHO-defined polycythaemia vera

·   Bone marrow fibrosis of grade 2–3 on a scale of 0–3

Additional criteria (two are required):

·   Anaemia (below the reference range, given age, sex, and altitude considerations) or sustained loss of requirement of either phlebotomy (in the absence of cytoreductive therapy) or cytoreductive treatment for erythrocytosis

·   Leukoerythroblastosis

·   Increasing splenomegaly, defined as either an increase in palpable splenomegaly of > 50 mm from baseline (distance from the left costal margin) or the development of a newly palpable splenomegaly

·   Development of any two (or all three) of the following constitutional symptoms: > 10% weight loss in 6 months, night sweats, unexplained fever (> 37.5 °C)

title: Thrombotic risk assessment (risk factors) in patients with polycythaemia vera {30848334}
copyright: Not necessary - table not in article
tablehtml:
Low risk:

·   Age < 60 years and no prior history of thrombosis {29515238}

High risk:

·   Age ≥ 60 years and a prior history of thrombosis {29515238}

·   Conclusions from the REVEAL study that was conducted in > 2500 patients with polycythaemia vera from US clinical practices [[Stein BL, Patel K, Scherber RM, et al. Mortality and causes of death of patients with polycythemia vera: analysis of the reveal prospective, observational study. Blood. 5 Nov 2020;136(Suppl 1):36–37. Doi:10.1182/blood-2020-137144.]]

·   The estimated 4-year mortality rate for patients with a mean age of ~66 years at enrolment was > 10%, and 33% of the deaths were attributed to thrombotic complications

title: Risk models for survival in polycythaemia vera (PV)
tablehtml:
Risk-stratified survival data from a large study at Mayo Clinic that included 665 patients with PV {30824279} based on a conventional risk model included age (≥ 67 years, 5 points; 57–66 years, 2 points), venous thrombosis (1 point), and leukocytosis (≥ 15 × 109/L; 1 point) {23739289}

 

Median survival time: High risk (≥ 3 points), 9.6 years; intermediate risk (1–2 points), 18 years; low risk (0 points), 28 years {30824279}

Three-tiered model: MIPSS-PV {31945802}

 

Hazard ratio–based risk factors:

·   Age > 67 years (3 points)

·   Leukocyte count ≥ 15 × 109/L (2 points)

·   Abnormal karyotype (1 point)

·   SRSF2 mutations (2 points)

·   Median survival time: High risk (≥ 4 points), 3.2 years; intermediate risk (2–3 points), 13.1 years; low risk (0–1 points), 24 years

Risk-stratified survival data from a large study at Mayo Clinic that included 665 patients with PV {30824279} based on a conventional risk model included age (≥ 67 years, 5 points; 57–66 years, 2 points), venous thrombosis (1 point), and leukocytosis (≥ 15 × 109/L; 1 point) {23739289}

 

Median survival time: High risk (≥ 3 points), 9.6 years; intermediate risk (1–2 points), 18 years; low risk (0 points), 28 years {30824279}

Selected risk factors (selected literature):

 

Substantiated

 

Age: > 65 years {15710945}, ≥ 65 years {29282357}, ≥ 50 years {34497324}

 

History of thrombotic events {12551821; 15710945; 20052743; 29282357}

 

Erythrocytosis: Haematocrit ≥ 45–50% significantly increased the risk of major thrombosis (CYTO-PV study) {23216616}

 

Described but not universally utilized

 

Leukocytosis

·   WBC count > 15 × 109/L {17614822; 17105814}

·   WBC count > 11 × 109/L {26206947}; WBC count ≥ 11 × 109/L {29282357}

·   WBC count in the range 9.5–25.0 × 109/L; systematic review and meta-analysis {31175128}

 

JAK2 p.V617F allele burden

·   JAK2 p.V617F VAF ≥ 75% was associated with major cardiovascular events (3.56-fold higher risk) {17625606}

·   JAK2 p.V617F VAF ≥ 50% increased the incidence of thrombosis by a factor of 4.632, as compared with JAK2 p.V617F VAF < 50% {31994332}

 

Arterial hypertension {29282357; 34497324}

·   Arterial hypertension increased the risk of thrombosis 2-fold, as compared with the group without hypertension in low-risk patients with PV {27737508}

 

Hyperlipidaemia {29282357}

 

Red blood cell distribution width (RDW)

·   Thrombotic-free survival was shorter when RDW was < 14% at diagnosis {34497324}

·   Thrombotic-free survival was shorter when RDW was > 15.6% {31669934}

 

Inflammation

·   Higher C-reactive protein was associated with increased major thrombotic events {21173097}

 

Major haemorrhage

·   Risk factor for thrombosis {29282357}

 

MIPSS-PV, Mutation-Enhanced International Prognostic Scoring System for Polycythaemia Vera; VAF, variant allele frequency; WBC, white blood cell.

title: Diagnostic criteria for polycythaemia vera
tablehtml:
Major criteria:

1.   Elevated haemoglobin concentration (> 16.5 g/dL in men, > 16.0 g/dL in women) or elevated haematocrit (> 49%a in men, > 48% in women)

2.   Bone marrow biopsy showing age-adjusted hypercellularity with trilineage growth (panmyelosis), including prominent erythroid, granulocytic, and megakaryocytic proliferation with pleomorphic, mature megakaryocytes (differences in size)b

3.   Presence of JAK2 p.V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation

Minor criterion:

·    Subnormal serum erythropoietin level

The diagnosis of polycythaemia vera requires either all three major criteria or the first two major criteria plus the minor criterion

aHaematocrit for diagnosis in the presence of a JAK2 mutation. In the absence of a JAK2 mutation, a higher haematocrit target (e.g. 52%) could be considered in men before further investigation is required. bMajor criterion 2 (bone marrow biopsy) may not be required in patients with sustained absolute erythrocytosis (haemoglobin concentrations of > 18.5 g/dL in men or > 16.5 g/dL in women, or haematocrit values of > 55.5% in men or > 49.5% in women) if major criterion 3 and the minor criterion are present.

Note: Determination of the red cell mass with 51Cr-labelled red cells allows the differentiation between true polyglobulia and pseudopolyglobulia. This is not a method for routine clinical use.
